findings.F1: Downside breaks in flat coins do not recover; they lean the other way at every horizon past one day. On closes below the prior 60-day low with a 60-day efficiency ratio at or below 0.3, the mean excess return is +1.23 % over 1 day (t 0.77, 81 cases on 35 days), -2.27 % over 5 days (t -0.76, 63 cases), -4.12 % over 10 days (t -1.01, 51 cases on 23 days) and -5.75 % over 20 days (t -0.78, 40 cases). The test's own -1.56 % (t -0.55) is this flat or negative effect, not a positive one too small to show.
findings.F2: The recovery is not graded by depth. On the recorded cases over 10 days, the shallow, mid and deep thirds earn -1.2 % (t -0.29), -3.2 % (t -1.05) and -1.3 % (t -0.22). Across all downside breaks the thirds are +0.7 %, -8.7 % (t -3.44) and -3.1 %. Depth does not order the outcome, which matches the step-5 slope t of 0.73.
findings.F3: The downside effect is mixed across periods and coins, with no part showing a clear recovery.

findings.F5: The upside continuation is graded by distance, but concentrated in time and coins.

ideas.idea: In a coin whose price has gone nowhere over the past 60 days, a daily close above the prior 60-day high is followed by a further rise over the next 5 days, and the further that close sits above the old high, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy, not fade, an upside break out of a trendless coin's two-month range, and buy more the larger the break, while refusing to short it as a failed breakout.
ideas.name: flat range upside break continues
